content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes are the edible fruits of the tomato plant (Solanum lycopersicum), native to South America and now cultivated worldwide. They have a juicy, slightly sweet‑tart flavor and a soft yet firm texture. Tomatoes are eaten fresh and are also used to make sauces, soups, salads, and countless other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically tomatoes are classified as berries, although culinary usage treats them as vegetables.
The heaviest recorded tomato weighed over 3.5 kg.
Lycopene gives tomatoes their characteristic red color.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
There are more than 10 000 tomato varieties, differing in shape, color, and taste.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes provide a generous amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular disease and certain cancers.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: Vitamins A and C in tomatoes help skin renewal and protect against UV‑induced damage.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood‑pressure regulation and proper muscle function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Tomatoes are low in calories, making them a great choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of tomatoes can aggravate gastritis or heartburn in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improperly washed tomatoes may retain pesticide residues; thorough rinsing before consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tomatoes can be eaten fresh in salads, sandwiches, and burgers, or used in sauces, soups, casseroles, and juices. Light cooking enhances lycopene absorption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store tomatoes at room temperature, away from direct sunlight, to preserve flavor and texture. For longer storage, they can be placed in the refrigerator, though this may alter taste and make the flesh firmer.
